_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Feature doors clear the inward vestibule cell so door_to_wall is 0
tasks.notes: LIVE FAIL after #146 (2026-10-27): facade_plan on jubilee_w93729745 / susu_w33830305 / west_w34391673 / retail_w33830236; susu/jubilee/retail re-applied still show 11 door_to_wall lower-half flags (susu 6, west 3, jubilee 2; retail 0). Doubles short: west 40-A/40-B, susu 42-C, retail 57-A plan 2-leaf but land 1-leaf ('no pair cell'). Cause: feature_build._set_door_leaf clears the outside stoop only — never the inward cell (opposite DIRS[face]), so the storey floor / solid behind the door keeps door_to_wall. Do not invent facade_plan or floor_offset hacks — fix the door clear tool. Deliver: _set_door_leaf (or its caller) clears the inward column at door height the same way as the outside stoop (air through the door opening; leave floor underfoot); unit test that a door with solid inward at b+1/b+2 is cleared and floaters.door_to_wall does not fire; re-apply affected features under site_lock --world southampton-build; west_w34391673 still mismatched (seq 196) — fix/re-apply as part of acceptance. Acceptance: site_patrol (or floaters) shows 0 door_to_wall on those four features; planned double leaves land as 2-leaf where the wall has a pair cell. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py. Prior notes about #146 absorbing this were wrong — #146 removed the old portal path but left the stoop-only clear.

tasks.title: Cell extract fetches the whole landscape set, and ground ignores culverts and tunnels
tasks.notes: Cause: the standard cell extract pulls buildings, highways and landuse only, so natural=water and waterway never reach the vector map; ground_sources.OSMGround sees 0 water columns and the water-body feature (#148) has no outline. Found 2026-10-27 on a mapped formal pool that was in no cached extract (a local-PBF query for the campus found it at once). A read-only audit of the same PBF against the cached clips (2026-10-27) found the same gap for every landscape family the planner layers already read: of the mapped features in the clip area, 0 barrier lines (fence, hedge, wall), 0 street-furniture points, 0 pedestrian-area polygons, 0 natural polygons (wood, scrub) and 18 of 20 leisure polygons were fetched. Deliver: (1) add water, waterway, barrier lines, furniture points, highway (pedestrian) polygons, natural polygons and leisure polygons to the standard per-cell extract step, so a new cell or world gets them without a manual run (the presets exist; the step does not call them; do not fetch kerb or crossing nodes); (2) one shared underground test used for every highway and waterway line in ground_sources: skip tunnel=* (any value), covered=yes, layer<0, level<0 and indoor=*; building_passage skipped only where it would not leave a hole at the surface; (3) hand mapped water polygons to the water-body feature as its outline source. Proof: unit tests on OSMGround: a culvert line (tunnel=culvert, layer=-1) and a stream line giving only the stream columns; a covered footway and a building_passage giving no surface columns; a natural=water polygon giving water columns; a fixture clip with one feature per fetched family round-tripping into the hedge, wall, fence, furniture, water and pedestrian sets; and a test that the cell-extract job list names every preset. No live-world test. Helps: any cell with ponds, streams, boundaries or street furniture, all worlds.

tasks.title: Trees layer reads mapped tree points and tree rows from the vector map
tasks.notes: Cause: OSMGround collects natural=tree points into .trees but no layer reads them; trees_layer takes lidar canopy plus the hand-read crown files only. natural=tree_row lines are not read at all. Deliver: use mapped tree points and tree rows as candidate crown positions in trees_layer (snap to lidar canopy peaks as #129 does; log each rejected point with its reason); tree_row lines laid as a crown sequence. Needs #156 so the points are fetched. Proof: unit test with a fixture cell holding three tree points and a canopy raster; every point inside the cell yields a crown or a logged rejection. No live-world test. Helps: any cell with surveyed trees, all worlds.

tasks.title: Ground reads pitch, playground, construction and allotment areas and their surface tag
tasks.notes: Cause: OSMGround._poly reads garden and park (as grass) and wood and scrub, and ignores leisure=pitch, playground, track, landuse=construction, allotments and natural=wetland, grassland, shrubbery; surface=* on polygons is not read either. Deliver: map these tags to a ground kind and priority, choosing the floor from surface and sport where tagged (e.g. tartan, asphalt, grass); keep landuse=residential, retail, commercial, industrial unread (they must not paint under houses). Proof: unit tests in the OSMGround fixture style, one row per tag asserting kind and priority. No live-world test. Helps: any cell with sports pitches, playgrounds or building sites, all worlds.

tasks.title: Building evidence carries roof, height and mapped entrance tags to the designer
tasks.notes: Cause: roof:shape, roof:levels and height are in the cached building clips but only building:levels is read (lidar_heightmap.map_levels); entrance=* points are not fetched, and the facade plan (#145) lists entrances from photos only. Deliver: put roof:shape, roof:levels and height in the feature evidence table as hints beside lidar (never an override); fetch entrance points and offer them as candidate door positions snapped to the footprint edge, ranked main before service and emergency. Proof: evidence-table unit tests with a fixture footprint carrying those tags, and a snap test for an entrance node. No live-world test. Helps: any building with mapped tags, all worlds.

tasks.title: level_pits fills wall-side voids next to footprints (S-019 / #155 live fail)
tasks.notes: Follow-up to #155. LIVE FAIL 2026-10-27: ground --apply on 48,-44 under site_lock planned 35 other pits then readback mismatches; seq 211 rolled back via site_recover. Tops at x 6145–6147, z -5520 stay y=36 vs neighbour (6144,-5520) y=44. Cause: (6146,-5520)/(6147,-5520) skipped by adj-to-footprint guard in level_pits; (6145,-5520) in a candidate component with bbox narrow=6 > PIT_MAX_WIDTH 5. Deliver: retune level_pits so free columns beside a footprint can fill to the outside rim (never raise footprint columns; never use footprint tops as the rim target). Raise PIT_MAX_WIDTH if the live 3-wide band's bbox needs it. Unit test: wall-side pit adjacent to fp fills to rim y; footprint columns unchanged; wide depression still skipped. Acceptance: ground rerun on 48,-44 under site_lock --world southampton-build; those three columns match y=44; no bad fill into footprints. Files: lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py. Helps: S-019 / I-015 void-beside-walls.

tasks.title: Readback ignores game-owned stair shape, so pitched roofs never reach built
tasks.notes: Was wrongly filed as a second #157 (id collision with trees). Follow-up to #149, same class as #66. Cause: pitched_roof_states (lib/builds/feature_build.py) sets each roof stair's shape explicitly (outer_left, outer_right, straight); the game stores a different shape, and block_store.same_state compares every property except the connection props of panes, bars, fences and walls, so stairs mismatch. Observed 2026-10-27: one pitched-roof feature read back 351 mismatches, 315 of them stairs (want outer_left/outer_right, got straight); cell_registry reconcile --fix repaired 0 of 315 and the feature stayed in-progress, which keeps its fixes (#149, #130, #132) from being judged on a built feature. Not verified: whether the game reshapes on placement or on a later neighbour update; what the other 36 mismatches are. Deliver: in lib/blocks/block_store.py same_state skip shape when the block id ends in _stairs (facing, half and material still compare); update the same_state docstring and the mirror note on site_kit.same; files lib/blocks/block_store.py and lib/blocks/test_block_store.py. Proof: direct same_state tests (stair planned outer_left reading back straight passes; different facing, half or material fails; non-stair with a different property fails) plus one reconcile/verify test through MemoryBlocks showing a feature with a reshaped stair reaches built. Live check: the next apply of that feature should leave only the 36 unexplained mismatches; list any left by block id and property and file them as a separate task.
